title: endpoint-templates-and-pin-policy-playbook
body:
Purpose:
A compact playbook describing: an endpoint template library, a template editor flow, and a policy-first model-version promotion ("pinning") editor. This is an opinionated set of wire descriptions + copy drafts aimed at reducing support friction during common deploy tasks (create endpoint, update model, promote variant).

Background / motivation:
- We keep getting: support tickets where customers accidentally overwrite an endpoint or expect a full rollback path and can’t find it.
- Teams want a simpler way to reuse endpoint configurations across projects (timeouts, batching, model family, token limits, safety filters).
- There is confusion between: "pin a version for safety" vs "promote a variant for performance". Need clearer language + an explicit policy DSL UI.

Goals:
- Make endpoint creation 60% faster for new users via templates.
- Surface the difference between temporary canary pins and durable promotions.
- Provide clear, inspectable policy rules with human-friendly copy and a single-click audit trail export.
- Avoid modal sprawl: prefer progressive disclosure panels for advanced rules.

Personas:
- Junior backend engineer: wants defaults, low friction, example templates.
- Platform/infra eng: needs reproducible templates, templated Git export.
- PM / Product owner: wants auditability and clear rollback.

Wireframe summary (three primary screens):

1) Template Library (entry screen)
- Top: search + filter chips (regions, instance class, model family, tags).
- Left rail: categories (Starter, Latency-optimized, Cost-optimized, Privacy/On-prem).
- Main: cards (name, short description, cost/latency estimate, "use" button).
- Card affordances: small eye icon -> preview, kebab menu -> duplicate/edit/delete, badge if shared org-template.
- Microcopy drafts on cards:
  - Title line: "Starter template — general purpose"
  - Subtitle: "Balanced latency and cost for dev and small-scale production"
  - CTA: Use template (primary), Preview (secondary)
- Inline quick-compare popover (select up to 3 cards) for side-by-side of key fields.

2) Template Editor (midflow, progressive)
- Top breadcrumb: Library > My Templates > Template X (autosave)
- Left column: key fields in a compact form (model family, instance type, autoscale min/max, batching window)
- Right column: advanced accordion panels (caching, kv-cache retention, token-limits, pre/post hooks, environment variables).
- Bottom: action bar with: Cancel, Export (YAML), Save-as-copy, Create endpoint from template (primary).
- Copy drafts for advanced accordion hints:
  - "KV cache retention: keep recent context to reduce cost for repeated prompts. Shorter retention => lower memory, faster cold starts."
  - "Batching window: time window to accumulate requests. Larger window improves throughput but may add latency."
- Validation: inline warnings (e.g., "Requested instance class unavailable in selected region").

3) Policy-first Pin/Promotion Editor (modal or slide-over)
- Top toggle: Mode = Temporary canary | Gradual promotion | Pin (durable)
- Central composer: rule list (ordered) where each rule is a human-readable block:
  - Trigger: on traffic % / tag / route / error rate / time window
  - Action: route X% -> model v2, fallback -> model v1, alert route owner
  - Conditions: only for requests with header X, or from route /chat/*
- UI affordances: slider for traffic %, small progress preview showing expected token-cost delta and latency change
- Microcopy examples:
  - Mode label explanation: "Temporary canary: short-lived test routing. Automatically retires after configured window."
  - Promotion tooltip: "Gradual promotion ramps traffic up based on health metrics you choose."
  - Pin tooltip: "Pin locks this endpoint to a specific model version until explicitly changed."
- Safety toggles: auto-rollback on error spike (threshold), notify on quality regression.
- Audit line at bottom: shows who created the policy, created_at, last_activity, and a single-click "Export JSON policy" button.

Copy experiments / microcopy playbook (short list):
- Primary CTA on endpoint create: "Create endpoint" vs "Launch endpoint" -> experiment variable A/B (Create favored by engineers).
- Pin affordance: small badge label = "Pinned (manual)" vs "Pinned (auto)". Prefer explicit parenthetical reason.
- Canary label: "Canary — temporary test" (help text: "Auto-reverts unless promoted")
- Error messages (example): "Unable to create endpoint: selected model not available in us-west1. Try a different region or a quantized variant."

Edge cases / guardrails:
- If a template references private model (customer-owned) and user doesn’t have access, show inline blocked state with link to request access.
- Prevent destructive rename of org-shared templates without at least 1 confirmation step and notifying owners.
- When promoting variant across hardware classes (GPU -> CPU), surface an explicit latency/cost delta and require override toggle.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Template Library screen with search/filters and 6 starter templates seeded.
- Template -> Create endpoint flow works end-to-end for hosted API usage.
- Policy editor supports: set mode, create 1 rule with traffic %, export JSON, and set auto-rollback threshold.
- Audit export includes rule history and user stamps.

Backlog (rough priority with Jira refs):
- JIRA-ENG-3880: Seed templates for Latency/Cost/Sandbox categories (P0)
- JIRA-UX-1421: Add quick-compare popover for template cards (P1)
- JIRA-SEC-774: Template permission checks and request flow for private models (P0)
- JIRA-ENG-3905: Traffic simulation preview for promotion editor (P1)
- JIRA-OPS-4112: Export-to-git templating endpoint (yaml) for infra reproducibility (P2)

Open questions / design decisions needed:
- Should the policy editor be a full-page experience or a slide-over? (tradeoff: discoverability vs modal noise)
- Do we show cost estimates for templates in tokens/min or dollar estimate? Both add complexity.
- Default template ownership model: personal copy vs org-shared? Most customers prefer org-shared with ability to branch.

Decision log (so far):
- Use progressive disclosure: template editor shows advanced fields collapsed by default (decided 2024-11-01).
- Exportable JSON policy will be the canonical artifact for infra and audit (decided 2024-11-15).

Next steps / immediate tasks (owners):
- Maya: prototype Template Library cards (Figma) — due 2024-10-18 (FIG-789)
- Luis: prototype Policy editor slider interactions (React sandbox) — due 2024-11-01 (DEV-214)
- Rina: write short help articles for pin vs promote (docs/knowledge base) — due 2024-11-04 (DOCS-58)

Notes to reviewers:
- Looking for quick feedback on the policy DSL readability (would someone unfamiliar with promos understand the rule blocks?)
- Also want sign-off on microcopy: default to "Create endpoint" CTA for now; if support metrics show confusion, switch to "Launch endpoint" in a follow-up A/B test.

Raw wire sketch references: Figma links are in linked artifacts PR (github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/221)

Rough transcript from last sync (snippets):
- Connor: "Users will accidentally leave a canary live. We need a clear expiration and alerting default."
- Rina: "Pin should feel intentional — make it a two-step confirmation with a short summary of impact."

End of doc.
